entities.summary: A strenuous wilderness traverse repeatedly dropping into and climbing above Finland's great northern canyon, with waterfalls, plateaus and river fords.
entities.description: Kevo alternates open Arctic plateau with abrupt descents into the canyon system, long stairs, river crossings and Fiellu waterfall. It is physically consequential rather than technically alpine, and reserve rules make timing non-negotiable: the marked canyon route is legal only in snow-free conditions from 15 June through 15 October.
entities.whyWorthwhile: A nationally singular canyon-wilderness journey whose repeated gorge reveals, waterfalls, fords and Arctic plateau are difficult to substitute elsewhere in Finland.

sources.title: Luontoon — Flooding on Kevo Summer Trail: current planning advisory
sources.note: Current advisory research, not a closure claim: the 31 August notice reported that the deepest of the three Kevojoki fords was about 68 cm on 28 August and that most trail sections had dried after recent rain. Metsähallitus says a separate red exception notice appears when the Roajjasjavri–Beahcelávojávrrit section is closed; that closure notice was not present on the current reserve feed at the 1 September check. Flooded fords cannot legally be bypassed off-trail, so hikers must recheck the live notices immediately before departure. The transient depth remains private research context and is not copied into canonical route facts.

variants.name: Kevo Canyon Trail — Sulaoja to Kenesjärvi
variants.description: The complete marked Kevo Canyon Trail from Sulaoja to Kenesjärvi. Its dense descriptive centerline is derived offline from the pinned 61-way OpenStreetMap subset of relation 6363386; the neighboring Guivi circuit and Sulaoja nature-trail branch are excluded.
variants.accessNotes: This remote point-to-point route requires transport between Sulaoja and Kenesjärvi and independent multi-day shelter. The four-day profile is a planning midpoint within the official 3–5 day range.
variants.seasonalLimitations: Walking the marked Kevo Canyon Trail is permitted only in snow-free conditions from 15 June through 15 October. Check current official notices immediately before departure because flood conditions can close the ford section.
suitabilityConstraints: For experienced, fit backpackers comfortable with repeated steep stairs, loose rock, long remote stages and multiple river fords.
Not suitable when a member of the party cannot safely ford moving water or comply with designated-route and camping restrictions.
warnings: Within the strict nature reserve, remain on the marked route and camp only at permitted sites; the legal hiking season is 15 June–15 October in snow-free conditions.

The route fords the Kevojoki three times and the Fiellujoki once. Flooded crossings cannot legally be bypassed off-trail: check live Luontoon notices before departure and use a backup route or turn back if a ford is unsafe or the section is closed.
Carry full remote-backpacking equipment, your own tent, river-crossing footwear, navigation backup and Arctic weather protection.
The Good Shit line is descriptive and non-navigation-grade; current signs, closures, weather, river conditions and Metsähallitus instructions take precedence.

entities.summary: A high-quality Sámi culture and northern-nature museum paired with an open-air trail of historic structures in the actual Inari landscape.
entities.description: Siida combines a modern permanent exhibition on Sámi culture and northern ecology with an outdoor heritage area of structures from different Sámi regions. The location in Inari is part of the experience, while weather and snow can materially change the outdoor half of a visit.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Cultural authority, excellent visual interpretation and an open-air collection in the Sámi homeland make this far more than a conventional regional museum.
